name: Great Lakes copper tools
summary: Old Copper communities around Lake Superior forged large working tools from naturally pure copper over several thousand years, one of the world's early metal-using traditions.
description: Large utilitarian tools forged from native copper; dated organic material remains embedded in some copper artifacts.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: An independent regional tradition of metal tools with only later ornament traditions as successors; scores imply tier 2, below the reviewed tier 1.

places.note: Lake Superior and western Great Lakes

date.label: c. 5570–4230 BCE, modeled onset (68% credible interval)
date.basis: Bebber et al. estimate the beginning of Old Copper practices at 7520–6180 calibrated years BP, 68% interval. The BCE values use BP=1950 CE and historical numbering; they are rounded display conventions. It is a probability interval, not a hard bound on actual onset.

events.statement: The dated copper-bearing Old Copper sites and directly associated remains support local use of worked native copper in the modeled historical horizon.
events.place_note: Lake Superior and western Great Lakes
events.population: Old Copper communities in the western Great Lakes
events.caveats: Bebber et al. report a 68% credible interval for a modeled onset, so a real onset may lie outside either limit. Associations and individual artifact manufacture dates remain uncertain; the interval is not a known-by claim.

evidence.locator: Introduction, Old Copper practice; Results, modeled start and Table 2
evidence.supports: Identifies the large utilitarian tools and reports the model of Old Copper site/tradition beginning at 7520–6180 cal BP (68%).
Reports embedded organic dates associated with 15 Old Copper artifacts; does not by itself date each artifact’s manufacture.

date.label: from c. 6550 BCE
date.basis: Rounded conversion of the reported 8500–3580 cal BP range for embedded organics, using the 1950 BP epoch; an evidence span, not the lifetime of one culture.

events.statement: Large utilitarian tools forged from native copper; dated organic material remains embedded in some copper artifacts.
events.place_note: Lake Superior and western Great Lakes
events.caveats: Associated organics date use indirectly. Sparse early finds and modeled cultural boundaries must not be equated; no claim of a global first.

community_entry.community: Old Copper communities in the western Great Lakes
community_entry.rationale: An approximate historical model of Old Copper practice is used as an explicitly probabilistic entry proxy; it is not a hard upper or lower date and does not use the modern excavation date.
community_entry.proxy_reason: Entry is inferred from dated copper-bearing archaeological contexts using a statistical model. This is a 68% credible interval for a modeled onset, not a certain historical date, hard bound, direct first artifact, or proof of the age of each embedded organic sample.
